Help: SONGS › untitled, about this page
┃ One song's settings. Up and down select one. [ and ] change it,    ┃
┃ Name: ENTER renames the song, which N on the Songs page does too.  ┃
┃ Tempo: in quarter notes a minute, unless a scene sets its own.     ┃
┃ Time signature: only changes what's drawn, the beats in the        ┃
┃ pattern editor and the bars in Live.                               ┃
┃ Scale: the set's scale its degrees play in, unless a scene sets    ┃
┃ its own; Bksp leaves it with none.                                 ┃
┃ Seed: none makes each export a new take; set one to repeat it.     ┃
┃ Groove: every clip's swing, unless a scene or track chooses.       ┃
┃ Live response: when an edit made while the song plays is heard: at ┃
┃ the next bar, at each clip's next pass, or ASAP.                   ┃
┃ Preview instrument: what Listen plays a pattern through.           ┃
┃ Visualizer: Arrange shows it first, over the File/Global page's.   ┃
┃ The Export row does the same as Ctrl+X, which works on every page: ┃
┃ it writes this song as a Live set or MIDI files.                   ┃

Help: PATTERNS › tune, about this page
┃ Each column is a step, as long as the step size. Tab switches      ┃
┃ between the piano roll and the rows. Home/End jump to the ends.    ┃
┃ Roll: Space or ENTER draws a note of the entry size (E picks); [   ┃
┃ and ] drag its end, X splits it, . sharpens or flattens it, G      ┃
┃ grabs, Bksp erases it, H picks its chord, K its keyswitches.       ┃
┃ Rows: Degree is a gauge: digits set it, [ and ] nudge it, as they  ┃
┃ adjust every number, Bksp empties the step. The rows under Octave  ┃
┃ come in sections headed by a row marked + (closed) or - (open):    ┃
┃ Space or ENTER opens or closes it, PgUp/PgDn jump between them.    ┃
┃ Basics: #/b, Velocity, Keyswitch. Chord: Chord, Tension, Scale     ┃
┃ (ENTER picks), Inv. Timing: Tie (Space after a note holds it),     ┃
┃ Gate (ENTER types one), Dot (d, t), Glide. Advanced: Probability,  ┃
┃ Ratchet, Ratchet Offset, Grab. CCs and Slide work on rests too.    ┃
┃ Use Draws adds the draws to notes and velocities.                  ┃
┃ S sizes the pattern, and on the rows I inserts a step and D        ┃
┃ removes one. M munges it. R reconfigures it: load over, step size, ┃
┃ time signature, drum on or off, direction, rename. L plays it at   ┃
┃ once, again and again, and stops it.                               ┃

┃ Every pattern in the set, which all of its songs share, in a tab   ┃
┃ Tab goes to the row of tabs and back; Left and Right choose a tab  ┃
┃ there; PgUp and PgDn choose one from anywhere.                     ┃
┃ ENTER edits the selected pattern; + (New) makes one in the group.  ┃
┃ A adds a pattern to the group, C copies, N renames, and renames    ┃
┃ G moves the pattern to another group. Bksp deletes it, once        ┃
┃ On the row of tabs: N renames the group, C copies all of it, Bksp  ┃
┃ L plays the pattern at once, again and again, and stops it.        ┃
┃ TIME is one play at the current song's tempo. USED counts the      ┃
┃ clips, in every song, and chains that use it.                      ┃
┃ / searches the list as you type: Tab completes, ENTER keeps your   ┃
┃ place, ESC goes back to the whole list.                            ┃

┃ Bypass When for a whole chain. Each line is a statement about a    ┃
┃ draw, such as AD odd. Each time a clip's pattern starts over, the  ┃
┃ statements are read, and when any is true the clip's notes go by   ┃
┃ this chain untouched for that pass.                                ┃
┃ Left and Right move between a line's parts and ENTER changes the   ┃
┃ part: the draw, the operator, and a number or another draw. A line ┃
┃ set to ignored does nothing. Bksp sets a line back to ignored.     ┃

┃ To delete a song's scale, clear it on that song's page first.      ┃
┃ Patterns that use degrees need a scale to export.                  ┃
┃ / searches the list as you type: Tab completes, ENTER keeps your   ┃

┃ A groove moves notes off the grid, like swing on a drum machine.   ┃
┃ It's a row of cells, one bar of 16ths to start with, each          ┃
┃ saying how late (+) or early (-) a note in that cell plays, as a   ┃
┃ percentage of the cell. Grooves follow time, not steps.            ┃
┃ The song chooses a groove, none by default, and a scene or a track ┃
┃ can choose another, or off to play straight.                       ┃
┃ The track's choice wins, then the scene's, then the song's, but    ┃
┃ The factory grooves are always there: four swings on 16ths, two on ┃
┃ 8ths and a push. ENTER looks at one and C copies it,               ┃
┃ but they can't be changed, renamed or deleted. A adds a straight   ┃
┃ groove of your own and opens it. On your own grooves,              ┃
┃ ENTER edits, N renames, C copies, M moves, S sorts yours by name,  ┃
┃ and Bksp deletes one that nothing uses.                            ┃
┃ / searches the list as you type: Tab completes, ENTER keeps your   ┃
┃ place, ESC goes back to the whole list.                            ┃

┃ Songs picks it, and Draws and Arrange work on it.                  ┃

┃ every key and F3 is about llamatron, on every page. Here O opens   ┃
